title: [Chapitre] IX et IX bis. [Ateliers] : notes manuscrites (05-15/07/1986).

deep.reconstruction:
Setting (as on pp. 64-67). A 'disposition' is a set E with a binary relation x|o|y. When the relation is symmetric, Grothendieck calls it a 'disjonction'. From the relation he gets polar operators:
- co-s-pr°(B) = {x : x|o|B}, a polar;
- s-pr°(A) = {y : for all x, x|o|A implies x|o|y}, the double-polar closure.
Σ_E is the lattice of closed ('polar') subsets. A correspondence α : E → P(E') induces α̅ on subsets.

The question raised on p.65 is whether α̅ is compatible with closure, i.e. whether B ⊂ s-pr°(A) implies α̅(B) ⊂ s-pr°(α̅(A)). It would suffice to have a correspondence in the other direction, β : E' → P(E), that is adjoint with respect to the relation:
(*) x|o|β(x') ⟺ α(x)|o|x'.

To look for an optimal β, he puts γ(x') = {x ∈ E : α(x)|o|x'}, which depends only on α. Then (*) says exactly γ(x') = co-s-pr°(β(x')).

This page draws the consequences. The condition means two things:
- 1°) γ(x') ∈ Σ_E, i.e. γ(x') is a polar.
- 2°) the closure of β(x') equals the opposite polar of γ(x') (written Cγ(x') = co-s-pr°(γ(x'))).
Hence an adjoint β exists iff 1°) holds for every x'. There is then a largest one:
β_max(x') = γ(x')^⊥ = {y ∈ E : for all x ∈ E, α(x)|o|x' implies x|o|y}.
Any admissible β has the same closure pointwise, so all of them define the same map E' → Σ_E (written Ψ_E). He also notes that β does not change if α is replaced by an α with the same closures, i.e. the same map into Ψ_E'.

The marginal NB says that for disjonctions (symmetric relation) the construction is symmetric: the β attached to α has α (up to closure) as its own adjoint. So the adjunction is an involutive duality on such correspondences.

He then starts a Proposition comparing Corr(E,E') (all correspondences) with the subset Corr dis(E,E') ('dispositional' ones), and crosses it out. On the next page he reformulates: morphisms are sup-preserving maps Σ_E → Σ_E', determined by maps E → Σ_E'.

Purpose: to set up a good category of 'dispositions' (Galois-closure structures from a relation), with morphisms that respect the closure lattices. This is foundational material for chapter IX ('Ateliers').
errors: In the explicit formula for the largest β, the image reads 'for all y ∈ E, α(y)|o|x' implies x|o|y'. With a non-symmetric relation the consistent orientation (y ∈ γ(x') standing on the left) is y|o|x. This is harmless only for disjonctions (symmetric relations), which is precisely what the margin NB addresses. Likewise, on p.65 he flags that he used symmetry x|o|y ⟹ y|o|x.
Condition 1° should say that γ(x') lies in the family of left polars co-s-pr°(B). Whether that family equals Σ_E depends on conventions that coincide only in the symmetric case.
The claim that this β is 'the largest' is correct: any β with β^⊥ = γ satisfies β ⊂ β^⊥⊥ = γ^⊥, and γ^⊥ itself works when γ is a polar. No substantive gap.

ideas.what: Polar/closure operators from a binary relation; lattice Σ_E of closed sets
ideas.modern_name: Galois connection of a relation / concept lattice / polarity (Birkhoff)

ideas.what: Adjoint correspondence β with x|o|β(x') ⟺ α(x)|o|x'
ideas.modern_name: adjointable maps between orthogonality spaces; Chu-space morphisms (relational version); bonds between formal contexts
ideas.usually_credited_to: Foulis-Randall (1970s, orthogonality/Dacey spaces); Barr/Pratt (Chu spaces); Ganter-Wille (bonds); Heunen-Jacobs, Paseka-Vetterlein (categories of orthogonality spaces)

ideas.what: Existence criterion: an adjoint exists iff each γ(x') = {x : α(x)|o|x'} is a polar; there is then a canonical maximal adjoint γ(x')^⊥, and all adjoints agree up to closure
ideas.modern_name: characterization of adjointable maps / closure-continuous relations
ideas.usually_credited_to: folklore in orthogonality-space and FCA literature

ideas.what: Morphisms as sup-preserving maps between closure lattices, determined by maps E → Σ_E' (next page)
ideas.modern_name: category of complete lattices with join-preserving maps; bonds ↔ sup-maps of concept lattices

missed.claim: Grothendieck's 'dispositions/disjonctions' with adjoint correspondences essentially reconstruct orthogonality spaces (Dacey spaces) and the Chu/FCA 'bond' framework. He does this independently, in the 1986 Ateliers notes, apparently without awareness of quantum-logic or concept-analysis work. The record does not link Grothendieck to this lattice-theoretic duality.

missed.why_it_might_matter_today: Of historical interest only: it documents Grothendieck working on relational and lattice foundations for a notion of 'space' in 1986. The mathematics itself is standard.

deep.surprise_reason: Correct but routine Galois-connection and adjointness bookkeeping, equivalent to known material on orthogonality spaces, Chu spaces and FCA bonds. The only interest is historical: Grothendieck independently developing this framework in 1986.
transcription_corrections: Explicit formula: '{α ∈ E | ∀y ∈ E, α(y) ‖ x' ⇒ x|0|y}' should read '{x ∈ E | ∀y ∈ E, α(y)|o|x' ⇒ x|o|y}'. The bound variable is x, not α, and '‖' is the relation |o|. The left side reads 'β(x') =' with x' overwritten.
Line 2°): likely 's-pr°β(x') = Cγ(x')  (= co-s-pr°(γ(x')))' rather than 'Sup pr°'. Here C denotes the opposite polar.
'Donc une telle β existe ssi on a 1°), et la plus grande ...'.
'Cette β semble "plus grande" des ...'; the following bracket reads roughly '[et en fait à une β quelconque, on associe la même fonction dans Ψ_E]'.
'Notons d'ailleurs que la β associée à α ne change pas quand on remplace α par des équivalents ... dans Ψ_E''.

The crossed-out Proposition reads: 'Soient (E,|o|_E), (E',|o|_E') deux dispositions. Soit Corr(E,E') l'ensemble des correspondances de E dans E', et Corr dis(E,E') le sous-ensemble des ...'. It says 'dispositions', not 'disjonctions'.

Margin NB: 'Si E, E' sont des disjonctions (x|o|y ⇒ y|o|x), alors on voit que la β associée ... est encore ... correspondance ... dont la associée est α'. That is, the construction is symmetric/involutive in the symmetric case.
